consensus_summary: Palm tree (tamar) primarily symbolizes the flourishing upright righteous (Ps 92:12) blended with victory/triumph of Christ and the redeemed/martyrs (palm branches in John 12:13 and Rev 7:9), with secondary notes on temple/Eden imagery, beauty, and wilderness provision.
book_summary: The palm tree is the righteous (quoting Ps 92:12-13 on flourishing when planted in the house of the LORD), carved beside cherubim in the temple, and held by the white-robed multitude before the throne; its branches are kappot (bent palms/fronds).
consensus_core_identification: the flourishing righteous (person/saints) who ultimately triumph
rationale: Both identify the palm's core referent as the righteous who flourish (Ps 92) and appear with palms in triumph/temple contexts (Rev 7; temple carvings). Book wording is more compact but covers the same primary strands and verses without narrowing, broadening, or replacing the referent; branch note and kappot detail are immaterial elaborations already latent in the consensus bases.
strongest_objection: Consensus sometimes treats tree-flourishing and branch-victory as technically distinct motifs, while the book unites them under one label.
